title: Microsoft Releases .NET 11: C# 15 Union Types, Native AOT CLI Host, and CoreCLR by Default in MAUI
gist: Microsoft shipped .NET 11 (STS, two-year support) with C# 15 union types, a Native AOT-hosted CLI, CoreCLR as MAUI's default runtime and agent/MCP tooling, while .NET 8 and 9 hit end of support and .NET 10 stays LTS. Developer reaction was mixed, with top comments saying AI coding tools have made new releases feel less exciting.

insights.claim: Microsoft released .NET 11 in November 2026 as a Standard Term Support (STS) release supported for two years, alongside C# 15, F# 11, ASP.NET Core 11, .NET MAUI and Entity Framework Core 11.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: STS cadence means enterprises standardizing on Microsoft's stack will likely stay on the LTS line rather than adopt .NET 11 broadly.
insights.quote: The release is a Standard Term Support (STS) version and will be supported for two years.

insights.claim: .NET 10 remains Microsoft's Long-Term Support .NET release, while .NET 8 and .NET 9 both reached end of support on November 10, 2026, the day .NET 11 shipped.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: End of support for .NET 8/9 forces an upgrade wave in Microsoft-shop enterprises, a tailwind for migration tooling and consultancies.
insights.quote: NET 8 and .NET 9 reached end of support on the same day, November 10, 2026

insights.claim: Developers on Reddit pointed out that .NET 11 and .NET 10 share the same end-of-support date, which weakens the incentive to move from the LTS release to the STS release.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Expect slower .NET 11 adoption; enterprise developers rationally stay on .NET 10 LTS.
insights.locator: On Reddit, the reaction was mixed

insights.claim: C# 15, the default language version for .NET 11, adds union types declared with a union keyword plus compiler-checked exhaustiveness for switch expressions, and closed hierarchies that restrict derivation to the declaring assembly.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: C# converging on functional-language features (discriminated unions) narrows a competitive gap with Rust, Kotlin, F# and TypeScript.
insights.quote: It adds union types, declared with the union keyword, and the compiler checks switch expressions over them for exhaustiveness.
insights.locator: C# 15 is the default language version

insights.claim: Developers welcomed C# 15 union types as a replacement for hand-written result classes, and System.Text.Json in .NET 11 supports serializing C# unions.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Union types are the headline developer-facing feature most likely to drive voluntary .NET 11 upgrades.

insights.claim: In .NET 11 the dotnet CLI starts through a Native AOT host by default and keeps the MSBuild server warm between invocations, targeting faster developer command startup.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Faster CLI loops matter more as coding agents invoke builds/tests repeatedly.
insights.quote: the CLI now starts through a Native AOT host by default and keeps the MSBuild server warm between invocations
insights.locator: In the SDK, the CLI now starts

insights.claim: .NET 11 raises minimum hardware requirements, moving the x86/x64 baseline to x86-64-v2, while the JIT removes more bounds checks and improves devirtualization.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Dropping pre-x86-64-v2 CPUs forces legacy hardware off newer .NET, nudging infrastructure refresh in older on-prem estates.
insights.quote: the x86/x64 baseline moves to x86-64-v2
insights.locator: The JIT removes more bounds checks

insights.claim: .NET MAUI in .NET 11 switches its default runtime to CoreCLR, keeping Mono available and Native AOT as opt-in, and stops shipping the Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility package.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Signals Mono's de-emphasis and consolidation of Microsoft's cross-platform client story on CoreCLR.
insights.quote: .NET MAUI now uses CoreCLR as the default runtime, with Mono still available and Native AOT as an opt-in option.

insights.claim: .NET 11 adds a dotnet new mcpserver template, .NET Skills for coding agents, and an experimental package of AI components for Blazor, embedding agent/MCP tooling directly into Microsoft's developer platform.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Microsoft is making MCP and agent integration first-class in its runtime ecosystem, reinforcing MCP as a de facto standard.
insights.locator: Other changes in this release are the dotnet new mcpserver template

insights.claim: Entity Framework Core 11 adds experimental vector search for SQL Server, along with fewer unnecessary joins and FullJoin translation.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Vector search in the default ORM lowers friction for AI/RAG workloads on SQL Server, defending Microsoft's database share against dedicated vector DBs.
insights.quote: adds experimental vector search for SQL Server

insights.claim: The most upvoted Reddit comments on the .NET 11 release argued that AI coding tools have made new programming-platform releases feel less exciting to developers.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Suggests AI coding assistants are diminishing the marketing pull of language/framework features, shifting platform competition toward agent integration.
insights.quote: The most upvoted comments argued that AI coding tools have made new releases feel less exciting.

insights.claim: .NET 11 libraries add Zstandard compression to System.IO.Compression, new Process APIs, JSON Lines output in System.Text.Json and a LINQ FullJoin operator.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Incremental library breadth; Zstandard adoption in a mainstream runtime extends the format's reach.

insights.claim: ASP.NET Core 11 generates OpenAPI 3.2 documents by default, a listed breaking change, adds asynchronous validation, and lets SignalR refresh authentication without reconnecting.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Default OpenAPI 3.2 output accelerates spec adoption across API tooling vendors.
insights.quote: generates OpenAPI 3.2 documents by default, which the release notes list as a breaking change
